title: Localized Bite Force and Functional Recovery of Masticatory Function Following Primary and Revision Endodontic Therapy in Older Adults: A Prospective Three-Arm Cohort Study
summary:
n this study, we investigate how masticatory function, chewing ability and the bite force generated during chewing changes in older patients receiving either root canal treatment or revision endodontic treatment of a tooth.
Three groups are compared: patients undergoing primary root canal treatment, patients undergoing revision endodontic treatment, and a control group without relevant dental pathology. In total, 75 participants are included.
Masticatory function is assessed repeatedly over a six-month period: before treatment (at the time of informed consent), immediately prior to treatment initiation, shortly after treatment, and at three and six months post-treatment. In the control group, measurements are performed at two time points over the same period.
Chewing performance is evaluated using a two-coloured gum test, while maximal bite force is measured using a dedicated sensor device. In addition, subjective chewing ability and further influencing factors, such as periodontal status, are taken into account.
The aim of the study is to determine how masticatory function recovers after endodontic treatment and whether it returns to levels comparable to those of healthy individuals.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Group A (25 patients): scheduled primary endodontic treatment of a posterior tooth
Group B (25 patients): scheduled endodontic retreatment of a posterior tooth
Group C control (25 patients): absence of any pathology requiring treatment
Exclusion criteria:
-Presence of severe systemic diseases with an impact on masticatory performance
-Presence of severe craniomandibular dysfunction
-Complete edentulism or insufficient occluding dentition and/or inadequate prosthesis retention
F-ailure to comply with scheduled follow-up (recall) visits
